questions.question: Consider this AlphaSimR simulation. Founders: 1000 diploid individuals from quickHaplo(nInd=1000, nChr=10, segSites=100), so loci start in linkage equilibrium. One purely additive trait with 10 QTL per chromosome (addTraitA: founder genetic mean 0, founder additive genetic variance 1). Residual variance is set once, at founding, so that narrow-sense heritability in the founders is 0.1 (setVarE(h2=0.1)), and stays fixed after. Each generation: phenotype everyone, keep the 100 with the highest phenotypes (selectInd, use='pheno'), and make 1000 progeny from random pairs of the kept individuals (randCross, one progeny per cross). What is the expected mean genetic value of the population after one generation, in founder additive genetic SD units (the founder mean is 0)? Answers within ±14% of the expected value count as right.
questions.answer_format: a single number (decimal, not a fraction or range)

key.theory: breeder's equation per cycle, Bulmer-reduced variance

questions.question: Consider this AlphaSimR simulation. Founders: 100 diploid individuals from quickHaplo(nInd=100, nChr=10, segSites=100), so loci start in linkage equilibrium. One purely additive trait with 10 QTL per chromosome (addTraitA: founder genetic mean 0, founder additive genetic variance 1). Residual variance is set once, at founding, so that narrow-sense heritability in the founders is 0.4 (setVarE(h2=0.4)), and stays fixed after. Every generation all 100 individuals are kept as parents (no selection) and make 100 progeny from random pairs (randCross, one progeny per cross). Many replicate populations are run independently from the same founders. What is the expected standard deviation, across replicates, of the population's mean genetic value after 5 generations, in founder additive genetic SD units? Answers within ±25% of the expected value count as right.
questions.answer_format: a single number (decimal, not a fraction or range)
